concepts.def: Describing your town or city: its size, location, amenities and what there is to do.
Talking about your region of the country, its features and how it differs from other areas.
Local and national transport, including public transport and how people get around.
Global problems such as poverty, climate change and conflict, discussed at the international level.
Poverty as a social issue, both locally and worldwide, and ways people try to help.
Volunteering and charity work, linking personal action to local, national and global causes.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Context 2: Local, National, International and Global Areas of Interest — a core area of GCSE French.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Context 2: Local, National, International and Global Areas of Interest brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Context 2: Local, National, International and Global Areas of Interest.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
